702724.t: Either from Proto-Hellenic *gʷīwos, from *gʷih₃wós (“alive”), and cognate with Old English cwic (English quick), Latin vīvus, and Old Church Slavonic живъ (živŭ); or a syncope of βίοτος (bíotos).

702745.t: From βοηθέω (boēthéō, “to help, assist”), from βοηθόος (boēthóos, “heeding the call to arms, rushing to battle”, Homeric).

702733.t: Denominal of βλαστός (blastós, “germ, sprout”). Origin uncertain, often compared to either βλωθρός (blōthrós, “tall”), which see, or German Blatt (“leaf, blade”).

702798.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gʷous (compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀦𐀃 (qo-o /⁠gʷōns⁠/)), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷṓws. Cognates include Old English cū (English cow), Irish bó, Latin bōs, and Sanskrit गो (gó).

702719.t: Attic corruption, possibly by assimilation, of βυβλίον (bŭblĭ́on).

702740.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gʷlépō, of unclear further origin.

702762.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *gʷorā́, itself from Proto-Indo-European *gʷorh₃éh₂, whence also Latin vorō.

702797.t: According to Herodotus, a Cyrenaic word; however, more recent research by Solmsen indicates a dialectal Doric origin instead.

702705.t: Borrowed from Middle Indic forms like Pali veḷuriya or Prakrit 𑀯𑁂𑀭𑀼𑀮𑀺𑀅 (verulia), from Dravidian, probably named after a city (modern day Bēlūr) in southern India in which the mineral was mined.

702792.t: From βούλομαι (boúlomai, “to wish; to will”) + -η (-ē, verbal noun suffix).

702749.t: This word and the synonymous βόθυνος (bóthunos) have been connected with Latin fodiō (“to dig”), Lithuanian bedù (“sting, dig”) and Middle Welsh beð (“canal”), assuming either a dissimilation of Proto-Indo-European *bʰodʰ- to Proto-Hellenic *bodʰ-, which…

702712.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gʷiā, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷey- (“to win”). Cognate with Sanskrit ज्या (jyā́, “overwhelming force; power; vanquishing”), ज॒य (jayá, “victory”).

702777.t: Perhaps from βοῦς (boûs), but it may be a loanword from an unknown source (such as Pre-Greek) that was associated with the native word secondarily.

702748.t: Shortened form of βοηθόος (boēthóos, “hasting to the cry for help”), from βοή (boḗ, “shout, call”) + θοός (thoós, “swift”, from θέω (théō, “run”)).

702772.t: From βόσκω (bóskō, “to feed, tend”) + -άνη (-ắnē, instrument noun suffix).

702732.t: Verbal formation from the same root as βλάβη (blắbē, “hurt, damage”), and traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *ml̥kʷyéti, from Proto-Indo-European *melkʷ- (“to damage”).

702722.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *gʷerh₃- Proto-Indo-European *-sḱéti Proto-Indo-European *gʷi-gʷr̥h₃-sḱé-ti Proto-Hellenic *gʷigʷrṓskō Ancient Greek βιβρώσκω From Proto-Hellenic *gʷigʷrṓskō, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷi-gʷr̥h₃-sḱé-ti, from…

702795.t: According to Beekes and LIV, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷel(h₃)- (“to want, wish”) (with no certain cognates), but with unexplained and pervasive o-grade in the present.

702775.t: Considered Pre-Greek, but also Semitic, relating to Hebrew בֹּסֶר (boser, “unripe grape”), Arabic بُسْر (busr, “unripe dates”), Jewish Babylonian Aramaic בֻּסְרָא (busrā), בּוּסְרָא (busrā, “unripe grape”), Classical Syriac ܒܣܪܐ (*busrā, “unripe grape”).

702727.t: From βίος (bíos) + -όω (-óō). Doublet of inherited ζῶ (zô).

702744.t: Of imitative origin, but the exact Proto-Indo-European root is unclear.

702741.t: According to Beekes, probably of Pre-Greek origin and cognate with βλέπω (blépō, “to see, to perceive”). Hamp had suggested Proto-Indo-European *gʷlep- (“to look”), though he offers no extra-Hellenic comparanda for such a root.

702739.t: From Proto-Hellenic *mləspʰāmos, from Proto-Indo-European *ml̥-s-bʰeh₂-mo-s, from *(s)mel- (“to deceive”) + φημί (phēmí, “to say”) + -ος (-os, adjective-forming suffix).

702743.t: From βοή (boḗ, “shout”) + -άω (-ắō). Possibly cognate to Sanskrit जोगु॑वे (jóguve, “to sound; to shout; to proclaim”).

702763.t: According to Beekes, probably of onomatopoeic origin. A connection with Armenian կորկ (kork, “dirt”) remains very doubtful.

702771.t: Unknown, but Beekes suggests a Pre-Greek origin in view of the suffix -υχος. Often connected with βότρυς (bótrus, “bunch of grapes”).

702723.t: Probably from Egyptian bꜣkt (“oil flask”). Beekes dismisses any relation with Latin fiscus (“basket”) and βαυκάλιον (baukálion, “jug, pitcher”).

702754.t: According to Beekes, the word is probably Pre-Greek, in view of the numerous variations and the suffix -ιτον (-iton).

702731.t: A nominal formation in βλαβ- (blab-), perhaps from an assimilation of an earlier form *βλαπ- (*blap-), based on evidence from Cretan forms (ἀβλοπής (ablopḗs) for ἀβλαβής (ablabḗs) and ἀβλοπία (ablopía) for ἀβλαβεία (ablabeía)).

702716.t: A reduplicated formation from the zero grade of Proto-Indo-European *gʷeh₂- (“to step, go”) with -άζω (-ázō), functioning as a factitive (causative) present meaning “to make or cause to go”.
